threads.body: `getBatchOperationName()` returns just "MULTI"/"PIPELINE" when the batch contains mixed command names. That contradicts the PR goal of deriving stable multi-command names in the form `MULTI <command>` / `PIPELINE <command>` and also loses useful detail for heterogeneous batches. Consider always appending a deterministic command name (e.g., the first command after `MULTI`, or the first pipeline command) when there isn't a single common command.

replies.body:
Handled in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/2fa9037e34de1ed8981d6de16ed18cd749a56fbd.

Redis database semantic conventions say mixed transactions and pipelines should use `MULTI` or `PIPELINE`, while homogeneous batches use `MULTI <command>` or `PIPELINE <command>`. I left the production behavior unchanged and added a regression test covering mixed `SET`/`GET` pipeline naming.
